title: import text: add IPv6 option, custom IPv6 addresses
description:
Add the option to use IPv6 instead of IPv4 for dummy headers,
including custom source and destination address, to the
"Import from Hex Dump" GUI box. Related to #16724

notes.body: The placement of the "IPv6" check box is not ideal. It's not a part of the radio buttons list, and it affects 5 of the radio button selections (not only IP). I think it should be moved. Maybe below the radio buttons list above "Maximum frame length"?

Hmm. What do you think about to the right of the IP protocol line edit, since it it is an IP option? The addresses (especially if IPv6) and the Export PDU dissectors need more space than the IP protocol, so the former span two columns whereas the latter is one column.
A couple of other options would be to figure out the address type automatically (and remove the IPv6 checkbox) or to put the IPv6 checkbox next to the IPv4 radio button.

> What do you think about to the right of the IP protocol line edit, since it it is an IP option?

That would make sense, as it's something that matters only if "IP" is the highest-level header to be generated by the import code.

However, calling it "IPv6" doesn't make it obvious that if it's *not* checked, the header is IPv4; perhaps it should be a combo box that offers options "IPv4" and "IPv6" rather than a check box.

> figure out the address type automatically (and remove the IPv6 checkbox)

What if no addresses are specified, so that the default addresses for the IP version in question are to be used?  We don't currently have default IPv6 addresses, but we do appear to have default IPv4 addresses (`IP_SRC` and `IP_DST`), and should probably have default IPv6 addresses as well.

(Also, text2pcap used 10.1.1.1 and 10.2.2.2 as the defaults, while the import code used and still uses 1.1.1.1 and 2.2.2.2.  Is there some reason why they were different, and is there some reason why one or the other should be preferred?)

> Also, text2pcap used 10.1.1.1 and 10.2.2.2 as the defaults, while the import code used and still uses 1.1.1.1 and 2.2.2.2. Is there some reason why they were different, and is there some reason why one or the other should be preferred?

My guess is that someone along the way decided that using RFC 1918 private IP addresses made more sense for default addresses (1.1.1.1 is registered to someone), and I think that's a decent reason to switch to the text2pcap defaults.

Figuring out the address type automatically also means adding some cross-validation logic to handle what if the source address is IPv4 and the destination is IPv6, or vice versa, and to warn the user appropriately. I suppose that could be done, but I don't see a good way around handling the default address issue, so I think I'm in favor of moving it to the right of the IP protocol line edit, and switching it to a combo box with IPv4 and IPv6 as options.

> My guess is that someone along the way decided that using RFC 1918 private IP addresses made more sense for default addresses (1.1.1.1 is registered to someone)

The change was made in 6e011bbf6e13c131be90721f3f48bea292555f1b:

```
Author: Bill Meier <wmeier@newsguy.com>
Date:   Tue Oct 19 16:13:48 2010 +0000

    Change dummy MAC addresses so we don't get Wireshark expert message:
    "[...] Source MAC must not be a group address: IEEE 802.3-2002, Section 3.2.3(b)"
    Specifically: use 0a:01:01:01:01:01 and 0a:02:02:02;02:02 (and dummy IP addresses
    10.1.1.1 and 10.2.2.2).
    
    svn path=/trunk/; revision=34571
```

ui/text_import.c was created in 296e43c3ebd6c7e8cfb50f0957dc487f5248bf2b

```
commit 296e43c3ebd6c7e8cfb50f0957dc487f5248bf2b
Author: Jaap Keuter <jaap.keuter@xs4all.nl>
Date:   Fri Nov 12 22:20:12 2010 +0000
    
    Add text import capability, like text2pcap, directly into the GUI.

    svn path=/trunk/; revision=34856
```

Perhaps the work on the GUI text import capability started before Bill's change, so that the code was copied from before the change, and didn't get picked up in text_import.c.

I went ahead and switched the IP addresses, since the text2pcap ones seem clearly better. 

!5632 is a proposal for using a combo box and moving the location. Adding a column doesn't make the entire widget larger, but it does make the line edits for the ports, ethertype, tag, and ppi smaller, which I think looks better, as they have relatively low maximum lengths compared to the export PDU dissectors and addresses.

This dialog does not look good on macOS in general, but the new position for IP version looks ok.
Remember to also disable the "IP version:" label when not adding a IP header.

![Screenshot_2021-12-28_at_23.29.31](/uploads/25ce628663090345d10d9b1b4fb1c669/Screenshot_2021-12-28_at_23.29.31.png)
